_schema: Every numeric entry is {v, unit, conf, src, note?}. Units: mm and deg (Blender machine frame: origin at the centre of the base footprint on its bottom face, +X left to right seen from the front, +Y toward the back, +Z up). conf: doc = stated in a document, standard or museum record; artwork = measured on the 1:1 MITS board artwork; photo = scaled from a photo; measured = measured on an original by the person named in src; est = estimate; design = our own choice where sources are silent. Source tags are defined in research/sources/bibliography.md. The sources give inches; each note keeps the inch value. version is the parameter set's own (each .glb records it as params_version).
reference_machine: MITS Altair 8800, 1975 (original front panel, 4-slot 88-EC expander boards, fan optional); research/REPORT.md

depth.note: 17.5 in; 18-18.5 in in other records, probably with rear parts; one measurement settles it

opening.note: 16.35 x 6.36 in; the visible panel as the photo shows it, centred in the box front; the name plate's lettering is placed from its left edge

lip_thickness.note: sheet steel of the case bottom's front frame

face_width.src: COMMONS-FP-CROMEMCO, MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #01; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
face_width.note: 0.19 in: the frame's front face, all round. Seen head-on the blue border is about 0.32 in, but most of that is the retaining lip, one recess deeper

recess_depth.src: MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #01, COMMONS-SI-UTHMAN; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
recess_depth.note: about 0.4 in: the frame stands this far in front of the dress panel; its inner walls run straight back to the panel, with no lip in front of it (a flange behind the panel's edge closes the gap)

return_depth.note: the front panel build shows only the front frame and a short return; the whole box models the whole case bottom

size.note: 16.469 x 6.531 in; 16 15/32 x 6 17/32 in, a loose original

grid_origin.note: 6.17 x 0.93 in; the A0 lamp, right of and above the centre of the visible panel; +-0.1 in

switch_hole_clearance.note: the hole clears the switch nut by this much all round, so the nut sits in it

gap.note: between the bezel's lip and the dress panel, and between the dress panel and the sub-panel: it is held between them, not fastened, and the model's parts never touch

row_z.note: height of each row above the A0 lamp

lamp_x.note: x from the A0 lamp, by the simulator's lamp ids; d* and status lamps in the upper row, wait, hlda and a* in the lower

switch_x.note: x from the A0 lamp, by the simulator's switch ids; s* in the switch row, the rest in the control row

bushing_diameter.src: APEM-5236 (1/4-40 thread), the modern equivalent of the American Switch ST-1-1-C

bushing_bore.note: room for the bat to swing inside the bushing

body.note: width x depth x height behind the sub-panel

bat_length.src: photos (MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #29, COMMONS-FP-CROMEMCO); APEM-5236; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
bat_length.note: from the pivot to the tip; shorter than the 13 mm first used

bat_radius.src: photos; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
bat_radius.note: at the base and at the head: slender at the bushing, thick and rounded at the end; a short round bat (1975), not the 8800a's flat handle

pivot_behind_bushing_front.note: the bat's pivot inside the bushing

momentary_hold.note: how long a momentary switch stays thrown before its spring brings it back

diameter.src: DFF180-PANEL hole size; Litronix RL-21 (no datasheet found)

proud.note: how far the dome stands in front of the dress panel

size.note: behind the dress panel, inside the bezel

length.note: 15.9 in; the two halves of the artwork are not stitched yet

lamp_label_above.note: 0.2 in: label centre above the lamp centre (0.16 and 0.23 in on the two photos)

switch_label_above.note: switch number (and the SENSE SW. line) above the pivot; moved clear of the switch nut's hole (r 5.0 mm) after a review against the photos, 2026-10-30; the photo gave 0.21 in

plate_text_size.note: cap height of ALTAIR 8800 COMPUTER (~0.43 in); the original face is a wide stencil-like display type, approximated

control_label_above.note: the upper command's line nearest the switch; moved clear of the switch nut's hole (r 5.0 mm) after a review against the photos, 2026-10-30; the photo gave 0.25 in

control_label_below.note: the lower command's first line; moved clear of the switch nut's hole (r 5.0 mm) after a review against the photos, 2026-10-30; the photo gave 0.2 in

group_bar_below.note: the bars grouping the switches in threes, under the pivots; moved clear of the switch nut's hole (r 5.0 mm) after a review against the photos, 2026-10-30; the photo gave 0.22 in

body.note: 10.0 x 5.0 in; length along the connector x height, tab not included

tab.note: 6.375 x 0.3 in; length x depth below the body

tab_from_front.note: 1.5 in; the short end of the card is its front

board.src: MITS-ASM-1975 printed p.65 (foil drawing, scaled by the pad pitch; research notes-boards-and-backplane §2)
board.note: 11.08 x 3.41 in; 88-EC: along the connectors (front to back) x across the slots

slot_pitch.src: S100-IEEE696; MITS-ASM-1975 printed p.65 (foil drawing, scaled by the pad pitch; research notes-boards-and-backplane §2)

first_slot_from_edge.src: MITS-ASM-1975 printed p.65 (foil drawing, scaled by the pad pitch; research notes-boards-and-backplane §2)
first_slot_from_edge.note: 0.59 in; board edge to slot 0's centre

connector_offset.src: MITS-ASM-1975 printed p.65 (foil drawing, scaled by the pad pitch; research notes-boards-and-backplane §2)
connector_offset.note: 0.3 in; the connector's centre sits this far toward the board's front from the board's centre, matching the card's off-centre tab

guide_spacing.src: MITS-ASM-1975 printed p.65 (foil drawing, scaled by the pad pitch; research notes-boards-and-backplane §2)
guide_spacing.note: 10.33 in; front guide to rear guide, centre to centre

guide.src: VCCA-GUIDE (an owner's measurements of an original); PLANET-KAUFMAN agrees
guide.note: across the slot x along the card x height; the original steps down to 9.5 mm wide and tapers to 7.5 mm deep at the top, not modelled yet

guide_slot.note: the channel the card's edge runs in

connector_body.src: SULLINS-CAT-2013 p.62-63 (a modern equivalent of the MITS part)
connector_body.note: 6.535 x 0.370 x 0.431 in: length x width x height above the board; ears 7.075 in over, holes 6.795 in apart (the MITS expander drawing: 6.80)

connector_slot.note: width x depth of the slot the tab goes into; no source gives the width; deeper than the card goes in

guide_top_depth.note: the guide's depth along the card at its top (16.75 mm at the base)

guide_cheek.note: how far the channel's cheeks reach past its floor toward the card's middle, at the base; they shrink with the guide's depth toward the top

board_centre_y.note: the seated cards' centre, front to back: the connectors sit midway between the rails (3.15 and 10.05 in behind the box front, +-0.15), and a card's centre is 0.3125 in behind its tab's; card front 0.9 +-0.3 in behind the D/C board

board0_right_edge_x.note: 7.25 +-0.15 in right of the centre line (1.25 in from the right outer face)

rail_section.note: flat bar 0.49 in wide (front to back) x about 0.125 in; the height is inferred from the 4-40 x 5/16 in screws

seat_depth.note: 0.265 in: how far the card goes into the connector; its body's bottom then sits about 0.47 in above the board

lift_out.note: how far a card rises to be out: its tab clears the guides' tops

lift_speed.note: how fast a card moves in and out on the page

rail_spacing.note: 6.85 +-0.12 in centre to centre, under the connectors' mounting ears (6.795 in apart); two modified machines show 7.1 and 7.25

tape.note: the tape under the expander board, so no land touches a rail; its thickness is ours

sheet.note: the steel of the lid and the tray

tray_wall_height.src: MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #03, #08; COMMONS-SI-UTHMAN; MITS_Altair_8800_microcomputer_-_Computer_History_Museum.jpg; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
tray_wall_height.note: 2.55 in: the tray's side walls, 0.1 in above the lid's skirts, which hide their tops

lid_skirt_bottom.src: MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #03; COMMONS-SI-UTHMAN; MITS_Altair_8800_microcomputer_-_Computer_History_Museum.jpg; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
lid_skirt_bottom.note: 2.45 in: how far down the lid's sides come; on the side the grey lid shows about 1.86 times the blue below it (7.0 / 2.86)

lid_front_gap.note: between the lid's front edge and the bezel's returns

lid_flange.note: the lid's rear flange, down behind the back panel, where its two screws go

louvres.src: COMMONS-SI-UTHMAN, MITS_Altair_8800_microcomputer_-_Computer_History_Museum.jpg, MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #01; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
louvres.note: a band of vertical slits along each side of the lid, about 4.7 to 6.6 in up (1.9 in long), from about 1 in behind the lid's front edge nearly to its back; counted roughly from the photos

chassis_lift.note: the chassis stands this far above the tray's floor (on its screws), so the two do not touch

width.note: 16.2 in over the side members' webs

flange.note: the side members' bottom flanges, inward

holes.note: the row of holes in each flange; the manual counts 13, 21 and 9 of them to the cross member and the rails

back_panel_y.note: the back panel's outer face, 16.9 in behind the box front

back_panel.note: width x height: 16.7 in, inside the tray's walls (the photo gives 16.85 +-0.2 in); the height is ours (it stands under the lid)

fan_hole.note: the fan opening, with a screen (the fan itself was the 88-FAN option)

io_cutouts.src: MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #03, #09; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
io_cutouts.note: eight DB-25 openings, 4 rows x 2, beside the fan opening on the side away from the transformers (4.46 and 6.80 in from the centre; 5.50, 4.39, 3.25 and 2.15 in up)

io_screen.note: the mesh screen behind the DB-25 openings, on the panel's inside

fan_screen.note: the square mesh screen over the fan opening, on the panel's inside (about 4.9 in)

cord_hole.note: the power cord's hole and grommet, 3.8 in right of the centre seen from the front, 1.5 in up

cross_member.note: its front face and top; the top is the weakest value (1.1 or 2.0 in, two methods disagree)

t1.note: centre x; width x depth (from the back panel) x height; it rests on the cross member. The photos put its top at 4.4 in, against T2's bottom at 4.3 in; the model makes it 3.0 in tall (top 4.1 in), so its coil clears T2 by about 9 mm. Separated after a review against the photos (2026-10-30): the three transformers stand apart, as in #07 and #09.

t2.note: above T1, against the back panel; its top 6.6 in up

t3.note: on its U bracket, left of T1 and T2; centre 3.86 in right, about 8 mm clear of T1 and T2. Separated after a review against the photos (2026-10-30): the three transformers stand apart, as in #07 and #09.

board.note: 8.35 x 3.0 in, on 0.375 in spacers on the cross member

terminal_block.note: two rows of ten, on the back panel between the fan's screen and T3

fan.src: MITS 88-FAN option; a 4.7 in muffin fan; MFE-SN220081K-PHOTOS #09; a review of the reference photos, 2026-10-30 (docs/3d-model.md, fidelity review)
fan.note: on the inside of the back panel, over its screen, centred on the fan opening; it hangs over the six filter capacitors

bundle_diameter.note: the laced bundle of the panel's bus wires

plug_unplugged.note: how far the data plug comes off the CPU's wafer, away from the card

power_cord_diameter.note: the AC cord; a short piece outside the back panel

paths.note: each unit's way out, as moves in the machine frame from its seated place; T2 parks forward of T1's way up, above the lifted cards

prereqs.note: what must be out before a unit can come out; the cards' own rules are in js/sim/box.js
